thread:
michael (oncall): hitting paging, 5xx surge from gateway -> lots of timeouts. getting alerts from synthetic checks and some customers reporting failures
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045. Pager notified: michael, lisa
jamie (sre): on it. quick check: scheduler queue depth trending up on region-us-east-1, batcher CPU high, many inflight batches not committing
kai (runtime): logs show a backlog of requests pinned to a small set of scheduler shards. looks like a scheduling hot trail - some shards have 3x normal queue length
michael (oncall): are these long-running generator calls or stuck KV-cache ops?
kai (runtime): mostly long generator sessions from streaming jobs + a few very large token requests. batch size growth + continuous batching is making these persist 
jamie (sre): customer impact: multiple mid-tier customers seeing >=50% request failures and 2-10s extra tail latency. support queue is lighting up.
customer-ops: flagged top 3 affected customers and opened bridge with CS. asking for ETA and mitigation steps
lisa (oncall-2): rollback options? can we fallback to smaller model or disable continuous batching temporarily?
kai (runtime): immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle long-running streams (evict by age), 2) reduce batch max size to 8, 3) route new traffic to standby pool in us-west-2.
jamie (sre): recommend: 1) evict inflight batches older than 12s, 2) temporarily cap batch size, 3) enable region failover for non-compliant tenants. I'll run eviction script now
michael (oncall): execute eviction, do cap, and open routing to standby. keep me posted.
jamie (sre): running:
```
# evict batches > 12s
curl -X POST 'https://internal-api/redwood/scheduler/evict' -d '{"age_s":12}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN'
# cap batch size
curl -X POST 'https://internal-api/redwood/config' -d '{"batch_max":8}'
```
jamie (sre): eviction started. seeing batch drain on shard-07. queue depth dropping from 240 -> 90
kai (runtime): switching routing policy: route-tier=non-critical -> fallback-us-west. patching in-flight rule now
incident-bot: Routing change applied: non-critical -> us-west-2 (rate-limited).
michael (oncall): notify support to tell customers we're mitigating and may see transient 429s while failing over.
customer-ops: message sent to affected customers, CS is monitoring. they asked if we have ETA to full recovery
jamie (sre): if evictions keep draining at this rate, tail errors should drop under threshold in ~7-10m. I'm going to keep batch_max capped for 30m and observe
lisa (oncall-2): what's our SLO breach risk? do we need a customer-facing incident page?
devex: prepare a short status blurb for the status page and post to #general if it'll be public.
michael (oncall): yes, prepare a short non-technical line + impact list. CS will use for customer comms
kai (runtime): one more note: root cause hypothesis — a traffic pattern (large streaming jobs) caused uncontrolled batch growth combined with a scheduler shard imbalance. continuous-batching heuristics failed to converge. need follow-up config hardening
jamie (sre): metrics update: 5xx rate from 18% -> 6% after evictions and cap. tail latency 95p dropped from 4.8s -> 1.2s. still monitoring.
incident-bot: Pager update: escalation level -> stable. Next check in 10m.
michael (oncall): good progress. keep the routing in place and batch cap for minimum 30m. start a follow-up ticket for runtime changes: shard rebalancer and batching thresholds
jamie (sre): creating follow-up: TICKET-1382 with action items: shard hot-trail detection, force-evict policy, continuous-batch safety limits, postmortem owner assignment
jamie (sre): postmortem owner: kai, timeline to draft: 48h
kai (runtime): ack. will attach logs and a small repro script showing how streaming + large batch_max triggers the stuck batches.
customer-ops: CS updated customers with ETA ~30m, asked to be notified when fully recovered
michael (oncall): status: all user-facing error rates below threshold, synthetic checks green. leaving routing + cap for 30m as planned, then we'll relax slowly
lisa (oncall-2): handoff to night oncall at 18:00. leaving notes and links to TICKET-1382 and the eviction runbook
michael (oncall): thanks team. final: assign postmortem and schedule a review with product to discuss guardrails for streaming jobs. closing incident channel in 1h unless regressions. :thumbsup:
